from collections import Counter


def transform(grid):
    # The repeated tile row reveals its fill color and the vertical lattice rails.
    common_row = list(Counter(tuple(row) for row in grid).most_common(1)[0][0])
    fill = Counter(common_row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    line_rows = [r for r, row in enumerate(grid) if row != common_row]
    line_cols = [c for c, value in enumerate(common_row) if value != fill]
    junctions = [grid[r][c] for r in line_rows for c in line_cols]
    rail_color = Counter(junctions).most_common(1)[0][0]

    # Each rectangular lattice cell is marked only when its four corners match.
    out = []
    for i in range(len(line_rows) - 1):
        row = []
        for j in range(len(line_cols) - 1):
            corners = (grid[line_rows[i]][line_cols[j]],
                       grid[line_rows[i]][line_cols[j + 1]],
                       grid[line_rows[i + 1]][line_cols[j]],
                       grid[line_rows[i + 1]][line_cols[j + 1]])
            value = corners[0]
            row.append(value if value != rail_color and all(v == value for v in corners) else fill)
        out.append(row)

    # Remove unused outer lattice cells while retaining blank cells within the pattern.
    active_rows = [r for r, row in enumerate(out) if any(v != fill for v in row)]
    active_cols = [c for c in range(len(out[0])) if any(out[r][c] != fill for r in range(len(out)))]
    if not active_rows or not active_cols:
        return [[fill]]
    r0, r1 = min(active_rows), max(active_rows)
    c0, c1 = min(active_cols), max(active_cols)
    return [row[c0:c1 + 1] for row in out[r0:r1 + 1]]

def transform(grid):
    """Decode colored corner pairs on a rectangular lattice into its cell grid."""
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])

    line_rows = [r for r, row in enumerate(grid)

    intersections = [grid[r][c] for r in line_rows for c in line_cols]
    rail = Counter(intersections).most_common(1)[0][0]

    for r0, r1 in zip(line_rows, line_rows[1:]):

            color = corners[0]
            row.append(color if color != rail and all(v == color for v in corners)

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    fill = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]

    # The puzzle is a regular lattice. Its horizontal and vertical rails are
    # the rows/columns mostly unlike the tile-interior background.
    line_rows = [r for r, row in enumerate(grid)

    line_cols = [c for c in range(w)
                 if sum(grid[r][c] != fill for r in range(h)) > h / 2]
    if len(line_rows) < 2 or len(line_cols) < 2:
        return [[fill]]

    # Ignore crossings: rail cells away from crossings reveal the divider color.
    rail_values = ([grid[r][c] for r in line_rows for c in range(w)
                    if c not in line_cols] +
                   [grid[r][c] for c in line_cols for r in range(h)
                    if r not in line_rows])
    rail = Counter(rail_values).most_common(1)[0][0]

    # A decoded pixel is colored only if the four corner crossings agree.
    decoded = []
    for r0, r1 in zip(line_rows, line_rows[1:]):
